name: Cell-level detection of weak E (thermal-noise bound)
driver_note: Any electrical sensing by a single cell responds to the in-situ electric field E, not to B. Theory sets the minimum detectable E; it is contested.
caveat: Weaver 1998 quotes B_min about 0.6 mT for a 0.3 m loop; recomputation gives 0.16-0.19 mT at 50-60 Hz, so do not reuse 0.6 mT without reading the paper. In-vitro effects at 0.5-1.2 mV/m (osteoblast, osteoclast work) sit 7-19x below the 9 mV/m bound and are not independently replicated in the retrieved set.

name: Subthreshold membrane polarisation (channel gating, network timing)
driver_note: dVm = 1.5*E*a (low-frequency Schwan limit). A 10 um cell at 0.0157 V/m (1 mT, 50 Hz, r=10 cm) is polarised by 0.24 uV, versus 18 uV rms thermal membrane noise and about 1 mV needed for ordinary gating.

E_Vm.basis: reported rms, rat hippocampal slice 50 Hz AC (Deans 2007)

confidence: medium for the arithmetic, low for network amplification
caveat: Slice work shows AC E of 0.18 V/m rms shifts firing timing in gamma oscillations (70 uV somatic polarisation). That is about 10-100x the E a 1-10 mT, 50 Hz coil induces on a limb.

name: Action-potential initiation (peripheral nerve, rPMS, TMS)
driver_note: Induced E, i.e. dB/dt integrated over the pulse (strength-duration law dB/dt_th = b(1+c/d)). B alone is not the variable. Geometry sets E (E = (r/2) dB/dt).

E_Vm.basis: reported (Wood 2008, Danner 2012) and computed (r=0.15 m for Bourland)

windows.margin: A sine of 1-10 mT at 10-100 Hz induces 0.003-0.47 V/m (r=0.10-0.15 m): 4x to over 1000x below 2 V/m. A 1 mT edge of 50 us gives about 20 T/s and reaches the rheobase range.

caveat: The 10-100 Hz band sits on the flat rheobase part of the strength-duration curve (within 13 %), so threshold does not rise sharply at low frequency except through accommodation, which no retrieved paper quantifies. Aδ/C-selective windows are not quantified in magnetic-stimulation papers.

name: Retinal magnetophosphenes (lowest-threshold ELF effect)
driver_note: Threshold set by induced E in retina with a 20 Hz tuning; B and dB/dt thresholds are not frequency-invariant, so neither alone is the dose.

B_mT.basis: reported, 50 % perception, whole-head (Fresnel 2026); rms inferred from dB/dt check

windows.note: No phosphene perceived at 100 Hz in the tACS comparison (Bouisset 2025).

caveat: ICNIRP CNS basic restrictions are set below this threshold. Values recalled from the ICNIRP 2010 text (public CNS 0.02 V/m at 50 Hz; occupational 0.1 V/m) are not retrievable from PubMed abstracts; verify before use.

name: Low-E in-vitro effects on osteoblast-like cells (response follows E, not B)
driver_note: When B was uniform and E varied across the dish or by cell orientation, response mapped to E. Direct E with no B also works. This is the best direct evidence that dB/dt (through E) can drive a cellular readout.

E_Vm.basis: reported rms (mV/m values converted from uV/cm)

evidence: in vitro, single group per effect
caveat: E is zero at the dish centre and maximal at the wall, so dish dose depends on geometry. Back-calculated effective radius is only a few mm. No independent replication retrieved.

name: Ion/ligand binding kinetics (Pilla configured signals)
driver_note: Pilla: burst duration and amplitude matched to Ca2+/calmodulin binding time constants set the bioeffect; retuning gave equal effect with 10x lower peak amplitude, about 800x lower average amplitude and about 10^6 x lower average power.

windows.note: Absolute E in V/m or mV/cm not reported in the retrieved abstracts. The task brief value 1-100 mV/cm could not be confirmed.
windows.B_uT_clinical_PRF: 1.0 G (100 uT) clinical signal and 0.02-0.05 G configured signals (Strauch 2007), pulse-modulated RF

evidence: mixed in vitro/animal, mostly one group
confidence: medium for the idea, low for numbers
caveat: Pilla clinical signals are pulse-modulated RF, a different regime from ELF coils. At an assumed 27.12 MHz carrier the dB/dt would be 3e2-1.7e4 T/s, showing B alone cannot rank dose across waveform families.

name: Which dose metric? (B, dB/dt, E, J, B*time)
driver_note: Electrical transducers follow E (hence dB/dt and geometry). Magnetic transducers (radical pairs, magnetite, static) follow B. Empirical amplitude windows change B and dB/dt together and cannot be assigned. No retrieved study varies rise time or frequency at constant B with matched E.
confidence: high for the logic, gap in data
caveat: At the same 1 mT a 50 us edge gives 20 T/s and 10x the E of a 500 us edge; 1 mT sine at 100 Hz gives 0.63 T/s. Report B_pk, dB/dt, waveform, geometry and computed E.
